findings.title: Denied delete attempts bypass the audit trail
findings.evidence: The guard exits via 'raise PermissionDenied' before the following audit.log call, so only successful deletions are recorded; an unauthorized or probing caller attempting to delete arbitrary user_ids leaves no audit entry, which is exactly the signal an operator would want for a destructive endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Log the denied attempt (actor, target user_id, timestamp) before raising, e.g. audit.log('user.delete.denied', user_id, actor=request.user) ahead of the raise, so authorization failures on the delete path are auditable.

findings.title: PermissionDenied symbol and 403 mapping not verifiable from the diff
findings.evidence: The guard depends on 'raise PermissionDenied' resolving to the framework exception (imported in this module) and on the project's exception handling mapping it to a 403; if the import is missing the handler raises NameError (500) and if no handler exists the delete endpoint returns 500 instead of a clean denial. Neither is shown in the diff.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the module imports PermissionDenied from the framework's exceptions (or add the import) and add a test asserting that a user without the delete permission receives 403/denial and that db.users.delete is not called.
